text: Refactoring is the process of improving your code’s structure without changing what it does. Imagine you have a messy room: you rearrange the furniture and clean up, but the room is still the same room. Similarly, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller pieces, or remove duplicate code. The key rule is that the program’s external behavior stays identical. Why bother? Because clean, readable code is much easier for you or your team to understand and modify later. This reduces “technical debt”—the hidden cost of messy code that slows you down in the future, making every change risky and time-consuming.
